sql_schemas: table leave_requests | fields: id, employee_id, leave_type, start_date, end_date, status, reason, manager_id, reviewed_at, review_comment, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | fks: employee_id -> employees.id; manager_id -> employees.id | indexes: employee_id: frequent lookups of all leave requests for a given employee; status: filtering by pending/approved/rejected status for dashboards and approval queues; manager_id: manager's pending-approval queue lookups; leave_type: filtering and reporting by leave type; created_at: time-range queries for reporting and history views

table leave_balances | fields: id, employee_id, leave_type, year, total_days, used_days, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | fks: employee_id -> employees.id | indexes: employee_id, leave_type, year (composite unique): enforcing one balance row per employee per leave-type per year; also the primary access pattern for balance lookups; employee_id: balance queries scoped to a single employee

table leave_policies | fields: id, leave_type, max_days_per_year, requires_approval, allow_negative_balance, is_active, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | indexes: leave_type (unique): policy lookup by leave type name is the primary access pattern; is_active: filtering active policies for dropdowns and validation

table employees | fields: id, first_name, last_name, email, role, manager_id, department, is_active, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | fks: manager_id -> employees.id | indexes: email (unique): login and identity lookup; role: RBAC enforcement queries (GP-005); manager_id: direct-reports lookups for manager dashboards; department: departmental leave reports and filtering

table audit_logs | fields: id, entity_type, entity_id, action, actor_id, changes, created_at | pk: id | fks: actor_id -> employees.id | indexes: entity_type, entity_id: audit-trail lookups scoped to a specific entity; actor_id: audit queries by user; created_at: time-range audit queries; action: filtering audit records by action type (CREATE, UPDATE, DELETE, APPROVE, REJECT)

data_notes: Five conceptual tables defined: employees (RBAC-ready with role, manager_id, department), leave_requests (core entity with status lifecycle and overlapping-date detection support), leave_balances (per-employee per-type per-year with composite unique constraint), leave_policies (configuration table for leave-type rules), and audit_logs (GP-002 compliance for all state-changing operations). Five repository interfaces with concrete pg Pool implementations: ILeaveRequestRepository/PgLeaveRequestRepository, ILeaveBalanceRepository/PgLeaveBalanceRepository, IEmployeeRepository/PgEmployeeRepository, ILeavePolicyRepository/PgLeavePolicyRepository, IAuditLogRepository/PgAuditLogRepository. All backings use the existing shared db connection (src/shared/db/connection.ts). Index rationale reflects access patterns: employee-scoped lookups, manager approval queues, status filtering, composite balance uniqueness, and audit-trail time-range queries.
